newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea allows securities firms to issue bonds.
newsitem.headline: South Korea allows securities firms to issue bonds.

text.p: South Korea will allow securities firms to issue three-year corporate bonds on their own behalf, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
He said securities houses might be allowed to issue bonds worth up to 100 percent of their equity capital, although a final decision has not yet been made on the ceiling.
But analysts said most brokerages would be reluctant to issue bonds due to the present high level of yields.
Corporate bonds are currently trading at around 12.5 percent, while brokerages extend margin loans to their customers at an annual interest rate of 11 percent.
